name: Jacobi plane-rotation symmetric eigensolver
definition: Choose p≠q with A_pq≠0 and orthogonal plane rotation G such that (GᵀAG)_pq=0; update A←GᵀAG and eigenvector accumulator V←VG until off-diagonal norm is small.
variables: A real symmetric matrix; G plane rotation; V accumulated orthogonal transformations
assumptions: Symmetry; systematic or maximal-element pivot selection and appropriate rotation signs; finite precision requires tolerance and iteration bound.
limitations: Repeated rotations can be costly for large dense matrices; clustered eigenvalues make individual eigenvectors nonunique or sensitive.
failure_conditions: Nonsymmetric matrix or unconverged off-diagonal residual
computation: Compute stable annihilating plane rotation, update symmetric entries and optional eigenvector accumulator.

source.citation: Golub and Van Loan, Matrix Computations, 4th ed., symmetric eigenvalue problem, Jacobi method; verify source before admission.

application: General symmetric matrix diagonalization for numerical analysis.
required_inputs: Real symmetric matrix, pivot schedule, convergence threshold, iteration bound.

name: Golub–Kahan bidiagonalization recurrence
definition: Start unit v₁, u₀=0, β₁=0. For j≥1 set w=Av_j−β_j u_(j−1), α_j=||w||₂, u_j=w/α_j; z=Aᵀu_j−α_j v_j, β_(j+1)=||z||₂, v_(j+1)=z/β_(j+1) when norms are positive.
variables: A real rectangular matrix; u,v left and right basis vectors; α,β bidiagonal coefficients
assumptions: Nonzero starting vector; exact-arithmetic orthogonality with finite-precision monitoring; stop on breakdown.
limitations: Loss of orthogonality and near-zero norms require safeguards; projected singular values are approximations.
failure_conditions: Unhandled zero norm or incompatible adjoint operator
computation: Alternate products by A and A transpose with coupled short recurrences.

source.citation: Paige and Saunders, LSQR: An Algorithm for Sparse Linear Equations and Sparse Least Squares, ACM TOMS 8 (1982), Golub–Kahan process; verify source before admission.

application: General reduced numerical representation of rectangular linear operators.
required_inputs: Linear operator, transpose operator, initial vector, dimension and stopping policy.
incompatible_methods: Treating partial projection as complete singular value decomposition
mechanism_note: Krylov recurrence rather than dense Householder bidiagonal reduction.

name: BiCGSTAB nonsymmetric linear-system iteration
definition: With r=b−Ax, fixed shadow r̂, ρ=r̂ᵀr, β=(ρ/ρ_old)(α/ω), set p=r+β(p−ωv), v=Ap, α=ρ/(r̂ᵀv), s=r−αv, t=As, ω=(tᵀs)/(tᵀt), x←x+αp+ωs, r←s−ωt. Set ρ_old←ρ at each completed step. Initialize p=v=0, ρ_old=α=ω=1; stop early with x←x+αp if s converges.
variables: A square matrix; b right side; x solution iterate; r,r̂ residual and shadow; α,β,ρ,ω scalars
assumptions: Nonsingular system; nonzero denominators and bounded iterations; residual checks and breakdown policy.
limitations: Irregular convergence and breakdown possible; residual alone may not imply small forward error.
failure_conditions: Zero or near-zero denominator, stagnation or nonfinite iterate
computation: Matrix-vector products, dot products and short recurrences; verify true residual before accepting convergence.

source.citation: Van der Vorst (1992), Bi-CGSTAB: A Fast and Smoothly Converging Variant of Bi-CG, SIAM J Sci Stat Comput 13, 631–644; verify source before admission.

application: General iterative solution of a nonsymmetric numerical system.
required_inputs: Matrix or operator, right-hand side, initial point, tolerance and iteration bound.
